title: Test data in automation: isolation and cleanup

videos.script: A test that passes on your machine and fails on the second run has usually met its own data. {{rerun}} This lesson is about the data a test leaves behind, and the data it finds. {{signup}} The shop gets a sign-up page. Your first test signs up Maria. It passes once. Run it again against the same server, and Maria already exists. {{unique}} So each test makes a name nobody else has. You compare four ways of making one. {{api}} Then you stop building the data through the form. Ten customers take a second and a half through the page, and under sixty milliseconds through the API. {{cleanup}} Then cleanup. A test that deletes what it made, at the end, is tidy until the run is killed halfway. A reset at the start does not care how the last run ended. {{basket}} And the basket. It is one list for everybody. Two tests at once see each other's fruit, and a reset only makes it worse. The real fix is in the shop. Until then, the tests take turns. {{privacy}} Last, where test data must never come from: real people. {{end}}
